title: The Epstein Next Door
author: Julia Yost
content:
![The Epstein Next
Door](https://www.compactmag.com/content/images/2026/02/4242_001--1--
page12.png)

You might have noticed that the internet has been more bonkers than usual
since about January 30. That's the day the Department of Justice dropped 3.5
million pages of new files related to the investigation of disgraced financier
Jeffrey Epstein, pursuant to the Epstein Files Transparency Act.

People are going crazy because they finally got their long-awaited evidence of
the long-rumored Zionist-financed global network of blackmailable pedophilic
cannibal elites. Right? More like the opposite. To find treasure in this
document dump, conspiracists are reduced to combining extreme literalism with
extreme interpretative license.
[_Literalism_](https://x.com/roddreher/status/2021525549232083275?ref=compactmag.com):
A rich man who acquires a Dutch Old Master painting of _The Massacre of the
Innocents_ obviously plans to hang it in his infant kill room.
[_License_](https://x.com/shellenberger/status/2022309428947521757?ref=compactmag.com):
A man whose emails sometimes mention "pizza" is obviously a consumer of
pedophilic pornography, or some other illicit pleasure starting with _p_.

Bonkers. Also boring, as Claire Lehmann complained in a
[_tweet_](https://x.com/clairlemon/status/2018064557265363245?ref=compactmag.com)
that got badly ratioed but wasn't wrong. To behold a popular mania and observe
over and over that it has no basis--nope, still no basis--sorry folks, still
no basis--wow, okay, still none--is tedious.

> "The ranks of the Epstein skeptics are growing."

Yet the ranks of the Epstein skeptics are growing. No longer are the
journalist [_Michael Tracey_](https://x.com/mtracey?ref=compactmag.com) and
the attorney [_Ted
Frank_](https://x.com/tedfrank/status/1884273369773699251?ref=compactmag.com)
waging a lonely war on social media, aided by a few writers such as [_Park
MacDougald_](https://www.thefp.com/p/what-the-epstein-fight-is-really-about-
trump-maga?ref=compactmag.com), [_Matthew
Schmitz_](https://firstthings.com/the-epstein-myth/?ref=compactmag.com), and
[_yours truly_](https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/the-epstein-
myth/id1823575411?i=1000720194837&ref=compactmag.com). Now they are joined by
liberals and libertarians such as
[_Lehmann_](https://x.com/clairlemon/status/2023601203440226316?ref=compactmag.com),
[_Robby Soave_](https://reason.com/2026/02/12/epstein-files-fuel-online-
outrage-at-figures-with-no-criminal-allegations/?ref=compactmag.com), and
[_Brendan O 'Neill_](https://spectator.com/article/the-epstein-scandal-has-
morphed-into-a-moral-panic/?edition=us&ref=compactmag.com); conservatives like
[_Barton Swaim_](https://www.wsj.com/opinion/the-real-epstein-
ring-f07d7b9e?gaa_at=eafs&gaa_n=AWEtsqcGtBQKMsWW_tycS3oXHCfiDyGs-H0LUuffH47FOA387gsFhQL2kHInSCe-
swM%3D&gaa_ts=6994e8bd&gaa_sig=YZfgihjnmCRqJZDe4Z_ar_mWJ_NSeIEmyOWV0mCjKAomSilTHlofGP8XXM3k0SAYi3OiMT3Ilwpv47eNnWHHMw%3D%3D&ref=compactmag.com)
and [_David
Harsanyi_](https://www.washingtonexaminer.com/in_focus/4448905/jeffery-
epstein-conspiracy-theories-idiotic/?ref=compactmag.com); gadflies like [_Alex
Berenson_](https://x.com/AlexBerenson/status/2020510913070067835?ref=compactmag.com)
and [_Richard
Hanania_](https://x.com/RichardHanania/status/2019903163139256621?ref=compactmag.com);
and new right figures including [_Inez
Stepman_](https://x.com/InezFeltscher/status/2022706064840384741?ref=compactmag.com)
and [_Pascal-Emmanuel
Gobry_](https://x.com/pegobry_en/status/2017504667345834087?ref=compactmag.com).

The latest file drop brought the Epstein story to a crisis. The desperation of
conspiracists who still aren't finding what they're sure must be out there,
the demands for unredacted documents and yet another 3 million pages of files,
the threats and condemnation directed at skeptics, have forced many to
conclude that this is just another witch hunt. A skeptics' discourse is
gaining momentum and confidence--a natural phase in the life cycle of a moral
panic.

I have given Epstein the epithet "disgraced financier," in preference to the
more [_popular_](https://www.cnn.com/2025/07/09/politics/what-to-know-about-
the-jeffrey-epstein-saga?ref=compactmag.com) "convicted pedophile," because
unlike the latter, it is accurate. Epstein was
[_convicted_](https://www.mtracey.net/p/was-jeffrey-epstein-a-convicted-
pedophile?ref=compactmag.com) in Florida of two crimes: solicitation of
prostitution, and procuring of persons under eighteen for prostitution. Those
persons were as young as sixteen. In 31 American states (though not Florida),
sixteen is the age of consent, reflecting the fact that sixteen-year-olds are
post-pubescent. They may, depending on jurisdiction, be victims of statutory
rape. But by definition, they cannot be victims of pedophilia.

Epstein-maximalist discourse thrives on an
[_expansion_](https://x.com/clairlemon/status/2020283946127487456?ref=compactmag.com)
of the term "pedophilia," such that in some quarters it now denotes any sexual
interest deemed exploitative or creepy. Thus, women who did "sex work" (as we
call it when we want to normalize it) for Epstein beginning in their twenties
present themselves as victims of child sex trafficking, and only the most
dauntless skeptics object. Surely, anyone who regards pedophilic crime as
uniquely grave must object to its being redefined to encompass the hiring of
adult prostitutes--redefined, that is, out of existence. Curiously, the
defenders of children against Satanic pedo-cannibals lap this stuff up.

What is going on? Kathleen Stock [_observes_](https://unherd.com/2026/02/the-
hypocrisy-of-the-epstein-panic/?ref=compactmag.com): "The depressing fact is
that sexual behaviour like Epstein's is absolutely standard in our society, in
the twin forms of prostitution and the pornography industry." We could use
less panic over Epstein, argues Stock, but more moralism. We could use a
realistic account of what ails our society--and it ain't Zionist blackmail
networks. America's internet pornography industry entails more labor
exploitation ("trafficking") of women than Epstein could have perpetrated in a
hundred lifetimes. Internet porn ruins the innocence of more children than
Epstein ever encountered, and it warps the sexuality of more adults than could
ever be recruited to any globalist cabal.

The Epstein panic, like so many moral panics, arises from an intuition that
something is amiss in our libertarian sexual settlement, if we could just say
what. Religious discourses would be helpful to this end, but they are
rigorously excluded from policy discussions. In the name of freedom and
tolerance, we have suppressed so much of our public morality that we lack
consensus terms for disapproving many forms of sexual conduct that
nonetheless, somehow, perhaps secretly, strike us as wrong: unseemly,
antisocial, diffusely harmful, destructive of discipline and virtue.

Moral panics are fits of line-drawing. They are not a resolution of our
confusions but a reaction to them; they are furious and irrational because
they are compensatory. In our fantasies of monstrosity, we establish with a
vengeance what is out of bounds and what is in. Trouble is, we are certain of
just two things: Children are off-limits; and _we_ are not monsters, because
we don't do the things Epstein did.

Except that if we confine ourselves to facts, it appears that [_lots of
us_](https://ifstudies.org/blog/how-prevalent-is-
pornography?ref=compactmag.com#:~:text=In%20the%20internet%20era%2C%20online,11%20percent\).)
do the things he did, just less opulently. Hence our need for "convicted
pedophile Jeffrey Epstein." Without him and his pedo-elite friends, we would
be left to confront the Epstein next door, or the one in the mirror.
